The main-text example, 0.1 M Bu4NBF4/DMF (κ = 4.76 mS cm−1, Table S7f) across a 5 mm gap at 100 mA cm−2, gives 12.98 V, of which 10.50 V is ohmic, 1.10 W cm−2 of heat and a passive steady state of 121 °C in the 100 mL beaker of §S6.1.
We close a lumped energy balance on a representative 100 mL cell with 10 cm2 electrodes.

For the compact cells σ is ≈7 for the microfluidic chip and ≈0.8 for an interior cell of a zero-gap stack; the two flow cells and the two rotating electrodes take the beaker value, and each value is given with its package geometry in Table S7i.
Each architecture is evaluated at its own median limiting current from Table S5.

Setting T_ss to the boiling point at each architecture's transport ceiling gives the required heat-rejection coefficient, U′_req = q(i_design)/(T_b − T_amb), which is compared with the three cooling classes of Table S7i and with the passive coefficient of each cell.

We bracket the effect: the lower end is κ fixed at 25 °C, the value used throughout §S6; the upper end is Arrhenius scaling of κ from 25 °C to the boiling point with an activation energy of 15 kJ mol−1 (Table S7i).
The resulting bounds on the reported quantities are given in §S10 (Tables S8 and S9), and the extrapolation of the rotating-cylinder correlation in §S3.3.
